definition: how a fear my body has learned either fades or gets confirmed

settled:
A bad thing landing below my safety line proves the alarm wrong. Above it, it proves the alarm right.

Ordinary social life delivers its punishment on a variable, random schedule, the kind that resists extinction hardest. So I will need a lot of safe experiences before I truly believe I am safe again.

An adverse experience is not safe or unsafe on its own. It is safe relative to my level. A high enough level absorbs a bad draw, and then being rejected and still being fine is the disconfirmation instead of a fresh wound. The world's response is not the only variable. My capacity to absorb it is the other, and it is the one I can raise.

What binds is the breach rate, the share of outcomes coming in above my line, held low for a duration.

One band is catastrophic whatever my level, and no level I could reach clears it. So raising my level can never take the breach rate to zero, and without raising it the rate never gets low enough either.
